summary: The client GET cache key must be stable for a given (path, params); sort the param keys before hashing so it never depends on Go's randomized map iteration order.
reason: cacheKey ranged directly over the params map, so the same request produced a different sha256 on each call. readCache almost never found the file writeCache had just written, silently defeating the 5-minute GET cache and forcing a fresh live request against Stingray's anti-bot gis endpoint on every homes/comps/listing/market/trends call — extra traffic that raises the 403/rate-limit risk seen in issue #698. This is a generated-client (client.go) template shape, so a reprint must re-apply the stable-key fix until the generator emits it.
validated_outcome: TestCacheKeyDeterministic (1000 calls, same params) and TestCacheKeyOrderIndependent now pass; before the fix both failed with differing keys across calls. TestCacheKeyDistinctParams confirms distinct region_id / path still produce distinct keys.
